children: Strong performance across oncology, biopharmaceuticals and rare diseases, alongside regulatory approvals and state-level healthcare partnerships, drives growth

AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited reported a 30 per cent year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 7,291 million in the second quarter of FY2026-27, covering July to September 2026, driven by sustained performance across its oncology, biopharmaceuticals and rare disease portfolios. The company also reported a 30 per cent increase in revenue for the first half of FY2026-27, reaching Rs 14,119 million, compared with Rs 10,854 million in the corresponding period last year. The company attributed its performance to operational efficiency, portfolio expansion and increasing adoption of innovative therapies addressing unmet medical needs in India.

Oncology remained the largest contributor, generating Rs 5,085 million in Q2, compared with Rs 3,978 million in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from biopharmaceuticals, covering cardiovascular, renal and metabolism (CVRM), respiratory and immunology (R&I), and vaccines and immunotherapies (V&I), stood at Rs 1,610 million, against Rs 1,268 million previously. The rare diseases segment recorded revenue of Rs 204 million, compared with Rs 38 million in the corresponding quarter last year.

Commenting on the results, Praveen Rao Akkinepally, Country President and Managing Director, AstraZeneca Pharma India, said the growth reflected the strength of the company's science-led portfolio and its ability to translate innovation into meaningful patient outcomes.

During the quarter, the company secured multiple regulatory approvals, including new indications for trastuzumab deruxtecan across HER2-positive breast cancer settings. Approvals were also received for benralizumab for hypereosinophilic syndrome and acalabrutinib-based combinations for previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and mantle cell lymphoma.

The company also expanded its healthcare partnerships through memoranda of understanding with the governments of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. These collaborations aim to strengthen oncology care, genomic testing and AI-enabled lung cancer screening across public healthcare facilities.

Other initiatives included K+ Connect, focused on hyperkalaemia management among patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease, and India Coronary Conquest 2026, aimed at strengthening cardiovascular care through clinician-led learning. AstraZeneca Pharma India also received recognition at the OPPI India Awards 2026 for its rare disease contributions and at the ETHRWorld Employee Experience Awards 2026, where it secured a Gold Award.
